# symbol-mcp

A Model Context Protocol server and CLI that tells an agent how to call something in a codebase: the signature, every parameter or prop with its resolved type, whether it's optional, its default value and its docblock, plus the file and line. It covers TypeScript, JavaScript and PHP, in the project and in installed packages.

This file is the manual for agents that call symbol-mcp's tools.

## TL;DR {#tldr}

- Four tools: `describe` (how to call one symbol), `list_exports` (what a package, file or namespace offers), `find_usages` (working examples from the project, and with `depth` the callers of those, to see what a change affects), and `status` (root and what's missing).
- Call `describe` before using a function, component, class or template you haven't used yet, instead of opening its source or `.d.ts` file. One call replaces reading the declaration, following its imported types, and finding its defaults.
- Props are flattened: `Omit<BaseProps, "id"> & { … }` comes back as one list of props. Props a component takes from the standard library or `@types` packages are summarized under the type the code wrote, such as `+ 269 more from Omit<AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement>, "onChange">`, which means it also accepts every `<a>` attribute except `onChange`.
- Every custom type the answer mentions by name (`ImageProps`, `TemplateArray`, `LinkData`) is defined once in a `types:` section at the end, closest types first, so one call covers types inside types. TypeScript's standard library types (`HTMLElement`, `Promise`) and React's own types (`ReactNode`, `CSSProperties`, `RefAttributes`) are left as names, since agents know them.
- Defaults come from the code (`{ size = "md" }`, `$args['size'] ?? 'md'`, `array_merge` with a defaults array) and from docblocks ("Default 'md'."). When they disagree, the code wins. For packages whose `.d.ts` dropped them, they're read from the package's original source.
- An answer that didn't fully resolve ends with `resolution: partial` and the reasons. Don't treat a partial answer's `any` types as the real types. A fully resolved answer has no resolution block; a `notes:` block appears only when something limits the answer.
- The project root is found automatically (§ Root). `status` shows which root is in use.

## Command index {#command-index}

| Tool | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `describe` | Signature, parameters or props, defaults, docblock and location of a symbol | (contract) name forms, lookup order, output format |
| `list_exports` | Every export of a module, package, file or PHP namespace, with short signatures | Pick something here, then `describe` it |
| `find_usages` | Where the project calls or renders a symbol, with the whole call or JSX element and the function it's in; `depth` adds that function's callers | PHP marks matches it can't confirm `[unconfirmed]` |
| `status` | Root and how it was chosen, and missing pieces | First thing to check when an answer looks wrong |

All four take `root` (one call only) and `format` (`text`, the default, or `json` for the full structure).

## `describe` {#describe}

| arg | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | The symbol. See § Name forms. |
| `from` | string | Narrow the lookup: a file path relative to the root, a module specifier (`@scope/pkg`, `./lib/api`), or a PHP namespace. |
| `language` | string | `typescript`, `ts`, `tsx`, `javascript`, `js`, `jsx` or `php`. The JavaScript and TypeScript names all select the same thing. Any other value is an error. |
| `depth` | integer 0-10 | How many hops of custom types to define under `types:`. Default: all that fit. 1 defines only the types the parameters use directly, 2 also the types those types use. 0 shows parameter types only, with no fields and no `types:` section. |
| `root` | string | Project root for this call. Usually leave it out. |
| `format` | `text` \| `json` | Output format. |

Without `language` or `from`, both languages answer, so a name declared in both returns both. That's useful for code with a TSX editor side and a PHP render side under the same name. With `language` or `from`, declarations in the other language are listed under `also defined in`.

### Name forms {#name-forms}

| Form | Example | Finds |
|---|---|---|
| Plain name | `Button`, `formatPrice`, `get_template_part` | Functions, components, classes, interfaces, types, enums, constants, variables |
| Member | `Cart.addItem`, `Cart#addItem`, `Cart::addItem`, `Cart->addItem` | A method, property or constant of a class (TypeScript accepts `.`, `#`, `::`; PHP accepts `::`, `->`) |
| Qualified PHP name | `Vendor\Pkg\Client`, `\Vendor\Pkg\Client` | A namespaced class or function |
| PHP template name | `notice` for `templates/notice.php` | A PHP file with no classes or functions, described by its file-level docblock and the keys it reads |
| File name | `Widget` for `Widget.tsx` | A default export with no name (`export default function (props) {}`) |

PHP names are case-insensitive, as in PHP. A plain PHP name that matches no class, function, constant or template falls back to methods with that name, up to 10 matches. Use `Class::method` or `from` to narrow it.

### Lookup order {#lookup-order}

TypeScript and JavaScript:

1. Top-level declarations in the project's files with that name.
2. Names imported by project files (`import { Button } from "@acme/ui"`), resolved to the package's declaration.
3. Only when nothing matched: installed dependencies (`dependencies`, `peerDependencies`, `devDependencies`) whose `.d.ts` files mention the name.

With `from`, only that file or module is searched.

PHP:

1. The project's `.php` files, except files ignored by `.gitignore` and the vendor folder.
2. Every path in Composer's autoload (`vendor/composer/installed.json`).
3. Only when nothing matched: every `.php` file under the vendor folder that declares the name. This finds packages Composer doesn't autoload, such as `php-stubs/wordpress-stubs`.

Project declarations are listed before dependency declarations.

### Reading the text output {#output}

```
## ImageDropUploader (component, typescript)
import from: "@acme/ui"
source: @acme/ui/src/ImageDropUploader.tsx (from dist/index.js.map)

ImageDropUploader({ image, onSelect, inlineSVG }: ImageDropUploaderProps): JSX.Element
params:
  props: ImageDropUploaderProps
      image?: string | number | ImageProps
      onSelect?: (image: ImageProps) => void
      inlineSVG?: boolean = false  // Render SVGs inline.
      + 1 more from RefAttributes
returns: JSX.Element

types:
  ImageProps { id: number | null; focalPoint?: FocalPoint }
  FocalPoint
      x: number  // Horizontal position, 0 to 1.
      y: number  // Vertical position, 0 to 1.
```

- `at:` is the declaration's `file:line`, shown for the project's own code. Symbols from installed packages (`node_modules`, Composer `vendor/`) leave out `at:`, the `[declared in]` of their fields and the locations of their members, because the agent needs the import path or qualified name, not the package's files. JSON output (`location`, `declaredIn`, and `dependency: true`) keeps them.
- `import from:` is the module the project already imports it from, so it's the path to use in an import. `source:` appears when docblocks and defaults came from somewhere else, such as a source map.
- Each field line reads `name?: type = default  // doc  [declared in]`. A `?` means optional. `= …` is the default as source text. `[file:line]` appears when the field is declared in another file than the symbol.
- Indented lines under a parameter are its fields: a component's props, an unnamed object type, a destructured parameter with defaults, or the keys of a PHP array described with hash notation or an inline `array{…}` shape. A field whose type has a name refers to it by that name.
- `types:` defines each custom type the answer refers to, once, closest to the signature first (the types the parameters use, then the types those use). Generics are defined in their declared form (`Transform<T>`); each use shows its own arguments. An object type with no docs or defaults prints on one line, `Name { a: T; b?: U }`. With docs or defaults, each field gets its own line. An alias of a union, tuple, function type or PHP array shape prints as `Name = …`, and an interface that only extends another type prints as what it extends (`TemplateArray = readonly Template[]`).
- `not listed (describe them for their fields): …` names the types left out because of `depth` or their size. Call `describe` on one of them for its fields.
- A fully resolved answer ends there. `resolution: partial` and its reasons appear when something didn't resolve, and `notes:` when something limits the answer (missing defaults, untyped JavaScript parameters, PHP usages marked unconfirmed).
- A named union type shows what it stands for: `classes?: ClassArg (string | string[] | Record<string, boolean>)`.
- `(type not declared)` marks a PHP array key that the code reads but no docblock documents. Its default still shows.
- Long inline object types are shortened to `{ … }` in the header when their fields are listed below.
- `members:` lists a class's public methods, properties and constants with one-line summaries. PHP classes list their own members only; describe the parent class for inherited ones.

## `list_exports` {#list-exports}

| arg | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `target` | string | A module specifier (`@scope/pkg`, `./lib/api`), a file path relative to the root, or a PHP namespace containing a backslash (`Vendor\Pkg`, or `Vendor\` for a single-segment namespace). |
| `language` | string | As for `describe`. |
| `root`, `format` | | As for `describe`. |

Each entry: name, kind, a short signature, the first line of its docblock, and its location. A TypeScript file that isn't a module (no imports or exports) lists its top-level declarations instead. A PHP `.php` path lists that file's declarations, and a namespace lists every indexed declaration in it and its sub-namespaces.

## `find_usages` {#find-usages}

| arg | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | As for `describe`. |
| `from` | string | Narrow which symbol is meant, as for `describe`. |
| `language` | string | As for `describe`. |
| `limit` | integer 1-200 | Most usages to return, and most callers listed under each function in a caller tree. Default 10. The header shows `showing N of TOTAL`. |
| `depth` | integer 1-10 | Levels of the caller tree. Default 1: only the usages. 2 also lists where each function containing a usage is used, 3 where those are used, and so on. |
| `root`, `format` | | As for `describe`. |

Each usage is a `file:line`, the function, method, class or template file it's in, and the whole enclosing call, `new` expression, JSX element or statement. That shows which props or array keys real code passes.

```
## formatPrice (typescript): showing 2 of 2

src/cart.ts:4  in total (function)
  formatPrice(item)
  ← src/checkout.ts:3  in checkout (function)
    ← src/checkout.ts:7  in Page.render (method)
      ← src/main.ts:3

src/price.ts:2  in formatPrice (function)  (callers listed elsewhere)
  formatPrice(-cents)
```

- `← file:line  in name (kind)` lines are callers of the function above them, one level deeper per indent. They show the location and the enclosing function but not the code; ask `find_usages` for that function to see its calls. Use a caller tree to see what a signature change affects before making it.
- A caller without `in` is top-level code (a script, a module body, PHP outside any function). `← no usages found` means nothing in the project uses that function, so it's an entry point the framework calls (a hook, a route, an export used by another package) or dead code. `← N more` counts callers left out by `limit` or the tree's size.
- `(callers listed elsewhere)` marks a function whose callers appear under another usage in the same answer, or the symbol calling itself. Each function is expanded once.
- Anonymous functions are looked through: a call inside `items.map(i => …)` or `array_map( fn … )` counts for the named function around it.
- TypeScript finds exactly that symbol, including through renamed imports. Import and export lines are skipped. Only project files are searched.
- PHP follows PHP's own name rules (namespaces and `use` imports) and works out the class of the object a method or property is reached through, so a same-name method of another class isn't listed. When the class can't be worked out (an untyped parameter, a `foreach` value, `global $wpdb`), the usage is kept and marked `[unconfirmed]`. A parameter type or a `/** @var Foo $x */` tag in the code confirms or rules it out on the next call.
- PHP also lists callbacks, marked `[callback]`: `[ $this, 'method' ]`, `[ Foo::class, 'method' ]`, `'Foo::method'`, and a function name passed where a `callable` is expected, such as `add_action( 'init', 'my_setup' )`. A function-name string inside an array (`'sanitize_callback' => 'my_fn'`) or passed to a function that isn't indexed is marked `[callback, unconfirmed]`. Read the shown call to tell a callback from a hook name; installing the framework's stubs package (for WordPress, `php-stubs/wordpress-stubs`) confirms the second kind.
- The callers of `[callback]` and `[unconfirmed]` usages aren't followed, since the function they're in doesn't call the symbol (a callback runs later) or may not.
- A template file is found through PHP strings that mention its path, such as `get_template_part( 'parts/ThemeHeading' )`, and through paths to it in the project's JSON and YAML files, such as `"render": "file:./Hero.php"` in a `block.json`. A global constant is found by name. Matches by name can include a different symbol with the same name (the result says so). A path PHP builds at runtime (`"$folder/$name.php"`) can't be followed, so a template loaded that way shows `← no usages found`.
- Project files are searched first, and dependencies only when the project has no usages.

## `status` {#status}

Takes only `root` and `format`. Returns the root and where it came from, and per language what's missing or replaced, such as no `tsconfig.json`, a missing `node_modules` or `vendor/`, or the bundled TypeScript.

## Root {#root}

The root is the server's configured root, else the client's workspace root, else the nearest folder above the server's working directory with `.git`, `package.json`, `composer.json`, `tsconfig.json` or `jsconfig.json`. `status` shows which one is in use. Pass `root` only to look at a different project for one call; switching back and forth is cheap after the first call.

## When parts of the project are missing {#missing}

| Missing | What the answer shows |
|---|---|
| `node_modules` | Project declarations still resolve. Types imported from packages show as `any`, and `resolution: partial` lists the imports. |
| `vendor/` | Project PHP still resolves. Types imported from Composer packages are named but not expanded (`partial`). |
| `tsconfig.json` / `jsconfig.json` | Default options; `status` says so. |

## Freshness {#freshness}

Every call sees the files as they are on disk: an edit or a new file shows up in the next call, and so do Composer changes. Files under `node_modules` are read once per server process, so restart the server after installing or updating npm packages.

## Recipes {#recipes}

**"What props does this component take?"**
```
describe({ name: "Button" })
```

**"Which component should I use from this package?"**
```
list_exports({ target: "@acme/ui" })
  → pick one
describe({ name: "MediaPicker", from: "@acme/ui" })
```

**"What keys does this PHP function's `$args` array accept, and what are their defaults?"**
```
describe({ name: "Card::render" })
```
Keys typed with a `@phpstan-type` alias, imported or local, have the alias defined under `types:`.

**"Show me how the project already calls it."**
```
find_usages({ name: "Button", limit: 3 })
```

**"What breaks if I change this function's signature?"**
```
find_usages({ name: "format_price", depth: 3 })
```
The first level shows each call with its arguments; the levels below show which functions reach it.

**"The editor component and the PHP template share a name. I only want the PHP one."**
```
describe({ name: "ThemeHeading", language: "php" })
```
The TypeScript declaration is listed under `also defined in`.

**"Is this a WordPress core function, and what does it take?"**
```
describe({ name: "get_template_part", language: "php" })
```
Works when a stubs package such as `php-stubs/wordpress-stubs` is installed.

## Diagnosis {#diagnosis}

**"No declaration named X was found."** Check `status` for the root first. Then try a member form (`Class::method`), a qualified PHP name, `from` with the module or file, or `list_exports` on the package to see what it actually exports. In TypeScript, a name that no project file imports is only found in dependencies whose `.d.ts` files mention it, so pass `from` for anything else.

**`resolution: partial` with "Imports that didn't resolve".** The listed modules aren't installed or their path doesn't resolve with the project's `tsconfig.json`. Types that come from them show as `any`, so don't copy those types.

**`status` says `(bundled)`.** The project has no usable TypeScript. Results can differ slightly from the project's own type-check if the project's compiler version is very different.

**A TypeScript answer is stale after `npm install`.** Files under `node_modules` are read once per process (§ Freshness). Restart the server.

**A PHP class is missing inherited methods.** Only a class's own members are listed. The note names the parent class to describe.

**A PHP usage you expected is missing.** Calls through a variable method name (`$obj->$name()`), `call_user_func` with a built string, and magic `__call` can't be followed. A callback registered in a config file (a YAML `_controller: 'Foo::bar'`) or by a naming convention (a Drupal `mymodule_form_alter`) isn't found either.

**The root is wrong.** `status` shows where it came from. Set `SYMBOL_MCP_ROOT` in the server's config, or pass `root` for one call.
